tex_content.html:
No $D_x$ is an embedded arc with both endpoints on $c_0$ and interior disjoint from $\partial A$.
Proof

↗ lem:geodesic-no-trivial-embedded-loop ↗ claim:local-embedding-of-geodesic-family ↗ claim:focusing-triangle-limit-existence ↗ cor:focusing-triangle-base-bound-collection ↗ rem:high-curvature-set-length-bound \sketch If $D_x$ cuts off a disk whose $c_0$-boundary has length at most one, Gauss–Bonnet contradicts its turning and area bounds. Otherwise apply the maximal-focusing construction to a unit subarc. Claims 6 and 6, together with the strip area bound, produce a set of length at least $0.87$ whose radials end on the disk boundary. One radial then cuts off a strictly shorter disk. Iteration eventually reaches the forbidden length-at-most-one case.

□
